apps.name: MyTrackpad
apps.subtitle: Wireless trackpad & keyboard for your Mac.
apps.localizedDescription:
MyTrackpad turns your iPhone or iPad into a wireless trackpad and keyboard for your Mac.

• Real multi-touch gestures: move, tap to click, two-finger right-click, two-finger scroll, pinch to zoom, and double-tap-and-hold to drag.
• Built-in keyboard, arrow keys and quick-function buttons (brightness, volume, media, Mission Control, Spotlight, dictation).
• Automatic discovery over Bonjour, plus a manual-IP fallback for networks where discovery is blocked.
• Native, minimal Liquid Glass design for iOS 26.

Requires the free companion app "MyTrackpad Server" running on your Mac (macOS 26+). Get it from the GitHub releases page.

versions.localizedDescription:
Smoother cursor and fixed gestures.

• Smoother cursor: full-rate (coalesced) touch sampling on iOS plus relative-delta injection on the Mac removes the stutter.
• Fixes a left tap sometimes registering as a right-click (a resting/grazing finger no longer counts as a two-finger tap).
• Hold an arrow (or Delete/Tab) to repeat it — keys now send press-and-hold with native auto-repeat.
• Mission Control and Zoom buttons work reliably (Zoom is now Zoom +/− using ⌘+ / ⌘−).
• New multi-finger gestures: three-finger swipe left/right to switch spaces, up for Mission Control, down for App Exposé. Pinch-to-zoom detection improved.
• New quick-function buttons: App windows, Prev/Next space.

Maintenance release.

• Fixes the macOS server failing to open (Gatekeeper “damaged”) and not appearing in the Accessibility list, by documenting a quarantine-free install (curl one-liner) and shipping a signed .zip.
• Same iOS app; rebuilt as 1.0.1.

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: MyTrackpad finds your Mac on the local network to connect and control it as a trackpad.

apps.name: Tesstats
apps.subtitle: Read-only Tesla stats — works with your self-hosted TeslaMate.
apps.localizedDescription:
Tesstats is a beautiful, read-only stats app for your Tesla, powered by your own self-hosted TeslaMate server.

• Live dashboard: battery, range, charging, climate, security, tire pressure, location.
• Trips with maps and consumption.
• Charging sessions with real charge curves (kW vs %SoC).
• Battery health and degradation over time.
• Rich statistics: trends, records, cost, CO2 saved, phantom drain, heatmap.
• Home Screen & Lock Screen widgets, a charging Live Activity, and Siri shortcuts.
• Notifications, multi-car, offline cache, encrypted backups, CSV/JSON/GPX export.

Tesstats is strictly read-only — it never sends any command to your car. It talks only to your own server (MQTT + TeslaMateApi), with everything encrypted by default.

Free and open source (AGPL-3.0): https://github.com/Drakonis96/tesstats

Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Tesla, Inc. or the TeslaMate project. "Tesla" is a trademark of Tesla, Inc. "TeslaMate" is a trademark of the TeslaMate project.

versions.localizedDescription:
Tesstats 0.3.1 removes the remaining loading stalls and makes every configurable section fully rearrangeable.

### Loading stays responsive
- Cache reads, JSON decoding, history aggregation and widget lookups stay off the main thread.
- Cached history remains interactive while fresher server data arrives.
- Large GPS traces are sampled before reaching MapKit, camera updates are debounced, and trip previews avoid repeated full-path scans.
- Parking derivation now scales linearly across drives and charges, with paginated rendering for long histories.

### Every section is yours
- Lists, filters, maps, totals and header cards can all be hidden or restored.
- Previously fixed Dashboard cards and the Stats date filter now participate in the saved layout.
- Parking has its own complete layout editor.
- Blocks can be moved with drag handles or explicit up/down controls, with stable accessibility identifiers.

### Verified
- 46 unit tests and the hide/reorder UI test pass.
- iOS and macOS builds compile successfully.

Sideload the attached Tesstats.ipa with AltStore or SideStore. The IPA is unsigned so AltStore can sign it, includes the widget, and omits the Watch app because AltStore cannot provision it. Requires iOS 18.

The interface no longer freezes while the app works through a long history — and there is something to look at while it does.

### Nothing blocks the interface
Every heavy calculation now runs in the background. Whatever has already been downloaded stays on screen and stays scrollable while the rest arrives, so switching to Trips or Stats on a multi-year history is instant instead of a stall.

Parking, Battery, Trips, Charging and Stats used to re-derive their analytics on every redraw, several times per screen, while the live MQTT feed was already redrawing. Deriving parking sessions and rebuilding the battery curve now happen once per real change, off the main thread. Scrubbing the battery and degradation charts is smooth again.

### A loading animation worth watching
While a section waits for its data it shows the Tesstats logo in its own centre, with speed trails rushing past it. Each block keeps its place and its heading, so you can see what is coming. Filters and range pickers stay live throughout.

### Cached history appears instantly
The offline cache is now read in the background and shown immediately on launch, before the server is contacted. A small "Updating…" badge floats at the bottom while fresher data is on the way — nothing is hidden and nothing is disabled while it loads.

### Also
- Charging drew its search and filter bar twice; now once.
- Settings → About links to the source code (AGPL-3.0).
- Added the non-affiliation notice for Tesla, Inc. and the TeslaMate project.

Sideload with AltStore. Requires iOS 18.

Rearrangeable screens, tappable units, tariff plans — and the app is finally translated end to end.

### Every screen is yours to arrange
Summary, Trips, Charging, Battery and Stats are built from blocks you can reorder or hide, from the ▦ button on the screen itself or from Settings. Defaults now lead with what most people open the app for — how the car is, and what it cost — with the enthusiast blocks further down.

### Tap to change units
Consumption switches between Wh/km and kWh/100 km, and tyre pressure between bar and psi, by tapping any value. Every value switches together and the choice is remembered.

### Tariff plans
Name a plan, give it price bands, and charging sessions TeslaMate did not cost are priced by when they happened. You set only when each band starts — the day closes itself, so the bands always add up to 24 h. Existing time-of-use setups are migrated automatically. Per-location prices can now be set from a charging session itself, which also explains where its cost came from.

### The app follows the language you pick
179 strings had never been added to the catalogue and always showed in English. Beyond that, dates, weekday names and chart axis labels are formatted from a locale rather than the string table, so a Battery chart could read `sáb / lun / mié` inside an otherwise English screen. Both are fixed, in both directions.

### It stops stalling
Every scrollable screen re-derived all of its analytics on each redraw. On a three-year history, one pass through Stats measured just over a second of blocked main thread — and the live feed triggers several a second. Screens now recompute only when something actually changed, and Stats does it off the main thread. The worst offender, the phantom-drain estimate, went from 948 ms to 4 ms. The launch splash no longer sits for a second and a half before showing anything.

### Maps follow the car
Drive somewhere new and the map stayed framed on the previous place with the marker off-screen. All four maps now re-aim: the live location, the history map after a filter change, and a trip's route once its real GPS trace arrives.

### Smaller fixes
- The trip row no longer breaks prices across two lines or truncates the efficiency label.
- A tariff plan could never be opened — the selection circle was swallowing the row's tap.
- The settings tabs and the gear button had no VoiceOver name.

---
Sideload the attached `Tesstats.ipa` with AltStore. The watch app is stripped from the IPA because AltStore cannot provision it.

Tesstats v0.1.7 — Sentry alerts that actually reach you.

If you never heard a Sentry alert before, this release is why: the notification existed but was easy to miss (default sound, silenced by quiet hours, re-firing on every banner repeat), and app-closed delivery via APNs is impossible on sideloaded installs. All addressed.

Sentry & security:
• Distinct bundled alarm sound and time-sensitive delivery for the possible-Sentry alert, so it stands out without looking at the phone.
• The Sentry alert can break through quiet hours (on by default) — that 3 AM warning is the one you want.
• 10-minute cooldown so one incident is one alert, not a burst.
• New optional "Sentry armed / disarmed" notifications from the reliable sentry_mode signal.
• Live Sentry-signal diagnostic in Settings → Notifications: see sentry_mode and the car's screen state update in real time, so you can confirm your TeslaMate emits the signal (arm Sentry, keep the screen open, walk up to the car).

App-closed alerts (the important fix):
• The optional push microservice now delivers through ntfy and generic webhooks, not just APNs. Sideloaded (AltStore) apps are signed without the push entitlement, so APNs can never reach them — ntfy (no Apple account, instant) or a Home Assistant webhook (sirens, lights, Telegram…) now cover that case. Server README rewritten around the three options; a 10-minute server-side Sentry cooldown matches the app.

Also: adding new notification preferences no longer resets your saved ones. Full English/Spanish localization.

Note: Sentry detection is inferred from the car's screen banner and TeslaMate polls every ~30 s, so very brief banners can still be missed. The video clip lives on the car's USB and is never available via TeslaMate.

Tesstats v0.1.6 — smarter costs, richer charts, faster sync.

New:
• Time-of-use electricity tariffs — define price bands by time of day (bands may cross midnight); unpriced sessions are costed by how much of their duration falls in each band. Recorded costs and per-location prices still win.
• Trip tags — label drives Work/Personal from the trip detail, filter the trips list by tag, and export the tag in CSV/JSON. Stored only on your device.
• Battery over time — a new 7/30-day state-of-charge chart on the Battery tab, reconstructed from drive and charge boundaries, with charging sessions dotted.
• Year-over-year overlay in the monthly trends chart (current year bars vs previous year line), for distance, energy, cost and consumption.
• Touch scrubbing — drag on the charge curve, degradation curve and monthly trends to inspect exact values.
• Activity heatmap now shows month labels, and tapping a day reveals its date, drive count and distance.
• Apple Watch companion app — battery gauge, range, state and charging progress, fed by the iPhone app. (Watch apps can't be provisioned by sideloading; the companion works when built from source via Xcode.)

Improved:
• Incremental history sync — automatic loads stop downloading as soon as they reach already-cached records, making refreshes much faster on multi-year histories. Pull-to-refresh still re-downloads everything.
• Battery health is now a main tab. The tab bar holds five real tabs (Summary, Trips, Charging, Battery, More) — six tabs previously made iOS hide Stats and the More hub behind a generic system list. Parking lives in More → Areas.
• Cleaner dashboard: brand logo moved into the toolbar, and the floating menu was replaced by a direct Notifications button.
• Decluttered More hub and removal of dead-end placeholder screens.
• Score rings are labeled (Efficiency / Drain / vs petrol) with VoiceOver support.
• The month-over-month card now states that it compares full calendar months.
• Switching tabs after a failed load retries automatically.
• Spanish translations for everything new, plus several missing ones.

Tesstats v0.1.5 focuses on a read-only visual upgrade.

- Adds a map-first dashboard with demo banner, contextual tutorial, last drive, 30-day efficiency and 48-hour activity timeline.
- Adds visual map/list views for trips and charging, including daily grouping, route previews, charge points and cost estimates.
- Adds a read-only Parking section derived from idle gaps, with live parking sessions and detail charts.
- Adds a local internal notification inbox with filters and persistence.
- Adds the More hub for read-only areas like stats, battery health, parking, notifications and future modules.

No remote vehicle commands, Fleet API control, automations, social features, Pro/paywall or Dashcam Studio are included in this release.

More from your TeslaMate data:
• Battery health now uses TeslaMate's official calculation (capacity & range, new vs now).
• Software update history — every firmware version with its install date.
• Charging efficiency and the energy lost to charging.
• Optional price per charging location for more accurate cost estimates.
• Peak regeneration record, plus per-trip regen and usable battery.
• Low tire-pressure warnings straight from the car.
• Fixed the cost trend chart, and the weekday chart now starts on Monday.

Themes & display polish:
• New light theme alongside the default dark theme (Settings → Appearance).
• Pick your accent color from 10 presets — it's applied across the whole app.
• Activity heatmap now spans the full card width, so its left and right margins match.

Accurate trip maps:
• Trip routes are now drawn from the real GPS positions recorded by TeslaMate, fetched per drive from TeslaMateApi — no more geocoding the address text.
• Fixes maps that landed in the wrong place when a city name was ambiguous (e.g. Toledo, Spain resolving to Toledo, USA).
• Elevation profiles now come from the actual drive trace too.

Connection robustness and clarity:
• MQTT host now accepts a plain hostname — any scheme or path you paste is stripped automatically (fixes a DNS resolution error).
• History API URL completes https:// if you omit it.
• Unique MQTT client-id per connection prevents a reconnect loop that made the status flicker.
• Clearer hints on the Server settings fields (host vs full URL).
• Full Spanish and English localization with an in-app language selector.
Initial public release.

apps.name: ScanKit
apps.subtitle: Scan, process, OCR and organize documents — all on-device.
apps.localizedDescription:
ScanKit is a native iOS document scanner built for power users who want full control over capturing, processing and exporting their documents. Everything runs on-device; nothing leaves your iPhone or iPad unless you turn on iCloud sync.

• Smart camera: live edge detection, auto-capture, manual corner adjustment with a zoom loupe, torch, zoom, framing grid, batch/continuous scanning and a book/pair mode.
• Powerful processing: color / grayscale / black & white (adaptive binarization) / auto modes, background whitening, deskew, perspective correction, full manual adjustments and reusable presets with live preview.
• On-device OCR (Vision): searchable PDFs, copy and extract text, search by document content, Spotlight indexing.
• Flexible export: searchable + password-protected PDF, JPEG / PNG / TIFF, plain text, batch file naming, and the native share sheet (AirDrop, Mail, Files, Print, Save to Photos).
• Organized library: nested folders with colors and emoji, tags, favorites, recents, trash, grid/list views, sorting, search and bulk operations.
• Adaptive design for iPhone and iPad, with Siri/Shortcuts and Home Screen quick actions.

versions.localizedDescription:
Working scan-mode switch + clearer color modes.

• Scanner: Auto / Manual / Double are now always-visible buttons that switch instantly (the old hidden menu felt unresponsive). “Double” captures a book/magazine spread and splits it into two pages; picking “Auto” always works even if auto-capture was set to Off.
• Color modes verified: Color is the original photo, B&W is adaptive monochrome, and Grayscale is now its own gentler look — clean page with the gray tones preserved, not a hard black & white.
• Combining or duplicating pages now keeps the full-color source, so switching a page back to Color still restores the original capture.
• Image export (JPEG/PNG/TIFF) now honors the chosen Resolution (DPI).
• Adding pages to an already-open document no longer opens a duplicate screen.

Interface polish + multi-select.

• Select multiple documents right from the main library (and Recents/Favorites): a new Select button, Select All, and a count in the title, then move / tag / export / combine / delete in bulk.
• Fixed icons (the OCR text panel no longer uses a chat-bubble) and more consistent spacing.
• Verified the page-preview edit controls (rotate, color, size, OCR, process, delete) work with progress feedback.

Editing in the page preview + responsive feedback.

• Tapping a page now opens it full-screen with the full edit toolbar: rotate, color, size, OCR, process and delete — all on that page.
• Color / size / process now run in the background with a progress indicator and a success haptic, so you can tell they're working (no more silent freeze).
• Page changes reflect immediately in the viewer and grid.

Color modes, scan sizes and safer trash.

• Color / Grayscale / B&W now work reliably — pages keep a full-color source and re-derive non-destructively, so switching back to Color restores the original capture.
• Scan size in Settings (Letter, A4, A5, A6, A3, Legal, Square…), default A4, plus your own custom sizes you can set as default.
• Change page size in bulk on selected pages (like rotate and color).
• Deleting from Trash now asks for confirmation.
• Cleaner OCR indicator icon.

Visual polish.

• Fixed document and page thumbnails overlapping / overflowing their cells.
• Removed the tiny status dots that looked like (un-tappable) buttons over each page.
• Cleaner icon-based toolbars in the page editor (Add / Select / Export, and rotate / color / process / delete when selecting).
• Clearer multi-select with checkmarks and Select All.

Bug fixes from device testing.

• Fixed scans coming out blank/white and rotated to landscape (camera orientation is now normalized before perspective correction).
• Fixed black & white / auto pages being blown out to pure white (rewrote the binarization).
• Page editor: clearer multi-select with Select All, rotate left/right on selected pages, and a quick color / grayscale / B&W switch per page or selection.

First public release of ScanKit.

• Full document scanner with live edge detection, auto-capture and manual corner adjustment.
• On-device image processing, presets, OCR and searchable PDF export.
• Folder-based library with tags, favorites, search and bulk actions.
• iPhone and iPad layouts, Siri/Shortcuts and Home Screen quick actions.

apps.name: Tempo
apps.subtitle: Rhythm, consistency and calm progress.
apps.localizedDescription:
Tempo is a minimalist habit and daily-activity tracker designed to actively encourage you to get things done.

• Daily goal that resets every day
• Habits with a 150+ icon library or custom emoji, accent color, weekday frequency, time of day and local reminders
• Two completion modes: tap to complete, or a timer (countdown/stopwatch) that fires a local alert and auto-completes
• Today view with a progress ring and live timer countdowns
• Schedule (hourly) view showing from what time to what time things are planned
• Weekly view with per-day completion and today highlight
• Native widgets (small / medium / large) with live timers
• Export & import all your data to move between devices
• Liquid Glass, light & dark mode, four languages (English, Spanish, French, Portuguese), fully local (no account, no network)

versions.localizedDescription: Full English, French and Portuguese translations, plus data export & import to move between devices.
First release of Tempo.

apps.name: HiperTracker
apps.subtitle: Gestiona tus listas de la compra
apps.localizedDescription:
HiperTracker es una app para gestionar listas de la compra que se conecta a tu propio servidor HiperTracker (autoalojado).

• Perfiles con PIN, listas personales y compartidas.
• Productos con icono, notas y varias tiendas.
• Tiendas del sistema (con logo) y tiendas personalizadas.
• Copia de seguridad completa (exportar/importar).
• Conexión segura: soporta servidores tras un reverse proxy con Basic Auth; las credenciales y los tokens se guardan en el Keychain y el JWT viaja en X-Auth-Token.
• Liquid Glass en dispositivos compatibles (iOS 26+).

versions.localizedDescription: Compartir listas con perfiles concretos: además de 'personal' y 'con todos', ahora puedes elegir qué perfiles ven cada lista. El administrador puede editar la compartición de cualquier lista.
Sección Tiendas: ahora se muestran primero los supermercados y después las demás tiendas, y se añade un buscador para encontrar tiendas rápidamente.

Arreglo: al editar un producto y cambiar de tienda, el cambio ya se guarda correctamente en iOS/iPadOS/macOS (antes se descartaba al volver del selector de tiendas). Crear, editar y eliminar funcionan con fiabilidad.
Sugerencias de emoji al escribir el nombre del producto (en español o inglés), selector de tiendas con los supermercados primero y logos de tienda más grandes.
Pull-to-refresh para forzar la actualización desde el servidor y logos de tienda más grandes en la lista.
Nuevo botón Cerrar sesión del login de la app: cierre completo (olvida tokens, login y configuración) y vuelve a la pantalla de conexión.

Seguridad del login de la app: rate limiting anti fuerza bruta, cabeceras de seguridad y secreto JWT robusto. El cascarón web queda protegido (página de login server-side). La app nativa no cambia su uso.
Login propio de la app: en Conectar activa 'Login de la app' e introduce usuario y contraseña. Alternativa al Basic Auth del proxy que evita los diálogos repetidos del navegador.
Se elimina el service worker (incompatible con Basic Auth + CDN): arregla las peticiones repetidas de credenciales y el bucle de recargas al iniciar sesión.
Arreglo de las peticiones repetidas de Basic Auth tras un reverse proxy / CDN: manifest con crossorigin=use-credentials y service worker servido sin caché.
Arreglos: 'Cambiar de perfil' abre siempre la selección de perfiles y el service worker deja de provocar peticiones repetidas de Basic Auth tras un reverse proxy.
Primera versión de HiperTracker para iOS, iPadOS y macOS.

apps.name: PaperQueue
apps.subtitle: Read more of your Zotero library, with less friction.
apps.localizedDescription:
PaperQueue turns your Zotero library into a focused, curated reading queue. Build a queue, mark papers as read, reorder by priority, search and add by DOI, and browse collections — all synced through Zotero tags so it works across your devices. On iPhone/iPad it's a companion for managing your queue; read the PDFs on your Mac in Zotero.

This build is unsigned — install it with AltStore/SideStore, which re-signs it with your own Apple ID.

versions.localizedDescription:
Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• Library filters reworked: each filter group (Authors, Tags, Year) now has its own search box, and the groups stay collapsed until you open them — only Tags is expanded by default — so the panel no longer unfurls everything at once.
• Fixed queue drag-to-reorder: a paper no longer snaps back to its old or last position when a background sync lands mid-drag.
• New “Move to position” button on each queued paper — type a number to send it straight to that slot.
• Sort the queue view: keep the real queue order (default), or sort by pages, year (newest/oldest), title, or author.

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• New AI mode — “Study a topic”: type what you want to learn, pick reference collections, and the assistant suggests readings to go deeper, based on the titles.
• The web app is now an installable PWA — add it to your home screen for a fullscreen, offline-capable app.
• Hardened for self-hosting: security headers (Content-Security-Policy, anti-clickjacking, nosniff) on every response.
• Smoother sync on large libraries: PaperQueue now honours Zotero's rate-limit (Backoff / Retry-After) signals.

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• Queues are now horizontally-scrollable tabs — drag a paper from the queue straight onto another tab to move it between queues.
• Faster on big libraries: the server caches a library snapshot (so fresh browsers load instantly) and the Library list is virtualized for thousands of items. The manual Sync button still forces a fresh pull from Zotero.
• A banner now tells you when a new version is available.

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• Cleaner model picker (Settings → AI assistant → Load models): a tidy alphabetical list instead of ragged chips, with a star to mark favourites.
• OpenRouter's huge model list is now grouped by provider (alphabetically), each section labelled.

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• AI suggestions/reordering now use each provider's structured-output (JSON) mode for more reliable results.
• Suggest with AI adds an "only papers tagged" include filter alongside the exclude filter.
• Keyboard shortcuts on the web (1–5 to switch tabs, / to search, r to sync, ? for help).

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• A spinner now shows on the "Loading PaperQueue" screen.
• Suggest/Order with AI show a live elapsed timer while the model works, and a long request no longer fails with a raw "aborted" error — it waits longer and gives a clear message suggesting a faster model.

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• Suggest with AI: the "exclude papers tagged" filter is now always shown and easy to find, above a height-bounded collection list.
• Minor copy cleanup in the web UI and docs.

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• Google Gemini is now a supported AI provider for the web edition (load models, pick favourites).
• Suggest with AI now passes your tags to the model and lets you exclude suggestions carrying tags you choose.
• Faster Suggest/Order with AI, and your settings (daily goal, queues, AI favourites) now follow you to any browser — including a fresh/incognito window.

Web edition only in this release — no functional changes to the iPhone/iPad app; the version is kept aligned across platforms.

• Order with AI now opens its model picker reliably instead of failing silently.
• Suggest with AI now keeps the picker visible and shows an immediate working state while suggestions are being prepared.

• PaperQueue now also runs in your browser — a new self-hosted web edition with the same reading queue, library, history and stats, kept in sync with this app through Zotero tags. Find it in the project's web/ folder (one Docker command, single port).
• Postpone now has a home: postponed papers move into a built-in "Postponed" list and wait there until you put them back in a queue.
• Version numbers are now aligned across iPhone, iPad, Mac and web. No functional changes to the iOS/iPadOS app itself in this release.

• Real-time sync — changes you make on your Mac (or any other device) now show up here within a second or two. PaperQueue keeps a live connection to Zotero and pulls updates the moment they happen, instead of only on a manual refresh, so moving between Mac and iPhone/iPad feels seamless.
• Much lighter, faster syncing — a refresh now fetches only what changed since last time (often nothing at all) rather than re-downloading your whole library, using far less data and battery.
• More resilient — the app refreshes automatically when you return to it, and a sync that hits a snag quietly falls back to a full refresh so your queue and read state never drift out of sync.

• Cross-device reading sync fixed — papers you mark as read on your Mac (or any other device) now show up on iPhone/iPad. Syncs always fetch the current state from Zotero instead of a stale cached copy, so a manual refresh actually picks up reads made elsewhere.
• Read/queue changes are no longer lost on a flaky connection or a version conflict: a write is retried instead of being silently dropped, and tag updates resolve conflicts automatically.

• macOS: drag-to-reorder in the Queue now works reliably — the double-click-to-open gesture no longer swallows the reorder drag, so you can grab any row and drag it to a new position.
• macOS: the Stats screen now lays its metric cards out as a clean grid of square tiles (icon, value and label centred) instead of stretched-out rectangles.

• Pages read — Stats now estimates pages from Zotero page ranges (e.g. 134–136 = 2, abbreviated 134–36 too): pages today / this week, total pages, a pages-per-week chart, and averages for both works and pages per active day.
• macOS: fixed drag-to-reorder in the Queue (a tap gesture was swallowing the drag), and the right-click menu now offers every action — mark read, read later, skip, remove, open, move to position and move to queue — alongside the visible buttons.

• Authors and editors are both shown now — an edited book or chapter that lists editors no longer hides the actual author. Editors are labelled (e.g. "ed."), and you can filter by either.
• New on Mac: Settings → Updates → "Check for Updates" downloads the latest version from GitHub, replaces the app and relaunches it automatically (falls back to opening the disk image if it can't).

More macOS polish and fixes:
• Library filters and Collections now open at a proper size — the author/tag/year lists and collection contents load instead of appearing empty.
• Settings no longer looks cramped; it uses a clean grouped layout.
• Clicking a paper selects it instantly — the previous selection lag is gone (double-click still opens it).
• The Library now shows the sync progress bar while refreshing, like the Queue.
• Bigger, hover-highlighted row action buttons with better spacing.

Bug fix: on macOS, the "Tags on read" picker in Settings opened empty — your Zotero tags wouldn't load. The picker sheet now sizes correctly, so the full tag list (searchable, multi-select) shows and the tags you choose are applied when you mark a paper read.

A much better Mac experience:
• Single click now just selects a paper; double-click opens it (no more accidental navigation).
• The reading queue shows large, always-visible action buttons on the right of each row — mark read, read later, skip and remove — so you no longer need fiddly swipes.
• History rows get visible buttons too (send back to queue, remove).
• The selected row is clearly highlighted.
These changes are Mac-only; iPhone and iPad keep their swipe gestures.

More control over your reading queue:
• Reorder by number — tap a paper's position badge (or use its context menu) and type the exact spot you want it in the queue.
• Position badges — every paper in the queue now shows its number under the icon.
• Scroll-to-top button — a floating button appears in the Queue, Library and History to jump straight back to the top of long lists.
• Custom tags on read — in Settings, pick one or more Zotero tags (searchable, with the option to add a new one) to apply automatically whenever you mark a paper read, on top of PaperQueue's own tag.

Gamification to keep you reading:
• Daily goal — set how many papers you want to read each day and watch a progress ring fill as you go.
• Streaks — current and best streaks reward consecutive days you hit your goal.
• Reading calendar — every day is coloured green when you meet your goal, orange for partial, red when missed; browse month by month.
• Richer Stats — read today / this week / this month, best day, daily average, plus a weekly chart with your goal line.
• Daily reminder notification at a time you choose, so you never break a streak.
• The widget now shows your streak and today's goal progress.
• Full-library sync fix — standalone PDF/attachment items are no longer skipped, so every item in your Zotero library appears.

• Full bibliography — PaperQueue now loads every item type in your Zotero library (books, book chapters, theses, reports, conference papers…), not just journal articles.
• Much faster sync — the library is fetched with parallel paging, so large libraries load far quicker.
• Sort the Library — order by recently added, oldest added, title, author or publication year, and your choice is remembered.
• Subtler, smoother animations throughout.

• Multiple reading queues — create personalized queues and switch between them (the Add button targets the Default queue unless you pick one).
• Library filters for author, tag and publication year, each with its own search bar, plus the existing status/collection filters.
• Queued papers now show a green check in the Library.
• A progress bar while your library is fetched.
• Cross-device sync for Mac local mode: add a Zotero API key under Settings → Cross-device sync so a Mac reading locally stays in sync with your iPhone/iPad.
Fixed false-positive "You appear to be offline" on pull-to-refresh, improved first-sync responsiveness with a loading state, and added pull-to-refresh to the Library tab.
